job_description_info.job_description:
# Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) – Patient Experience

**Company:** Verdane Care (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Graz, Austria (hybrid) or fully remote within Austria, Germany, Croatia or Slovenia
**Employment:** Full-time, permanent (or B2B contract in Croatia on request)
**Team:** Patient Experience squad (4 engineers, 1 designer, 1 product manager)

## About the role

Verdane Care makes appointment-booking and follow-up software for private clinics and physiotherapy practices. Patients use our web app and mobile web experience to book visits, fill in intake forms, receive reminders and view exercise plans.

As a Full-Stack Engineer you will build and improve those patient-facing features end to end – from React components and accessibility to the Node.js APIs and the database behind them. You will work in a small squad with a designer and a product manager, and you will ship to production several times a week.

## What you will do

- Build new patient-facing features in React and TypeScript, with a strong focus on accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) and performance on low-end phones
- Implement Node.js (NestJS) APIs and PostgreSQL schemas to support those features
- Integrate with third-party systems such as clinic calendars, SMS providers and payment gateways
- Write unit, integration and end-to-end tests (Jest, Playwright) and keep the build green
- Take part in design reviews, usability sessions and sprint planning
- Handle personal health data responsibly: follow our GDPR and data-minimisation guidelines, support audit requests from clinic customers
- Mentor interns or junior colleagues when the opportunity arises

## What you bring

**Must have**
- 2+ years of professional experience building web applications with React and TypeScript
- Experience writing backend services in Node.js (Express, NestJS or similar) and working with SQL databases
- Understanding of semantic HTML, responsive layouts and web accessibility basics
- Experience with automated testing (unit and end-to-end) and Git-based workflows
- Awareness of web security fundamentals (authentication, OWASP Top 10) and willingness to learn the privacy requirements of health data
- Fluent English; German or Croatian is helpful for customer-facing conversations

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Next.js or other server-side rendering frameworks
- Experience in healthcare, wellness or other regulated environments
- Familiarity with AWS or a similar cloud, and with Docker
- Experience with design systems and Storybook
- Experience with analytics and A/B testing

## What we offer

- Salary range EUR 54,000 – 70,000 gross per year depending on experience (Austrian collective agreement minimum applies)
- 25 days of holiday plus the Austrian public holidays, 5 additional well-being days and a EUR 1,200 yearly education budget
- Flexible hours, a home-office stipend and a yearly team retreat
- A friendly, low-ego team that cares about the people who use our software

## How to apply

Send your CV. A short cover letter and a link to something you have built (a portfolio, a GitHub project or a live site) are welcome but optional. We reply within ten working days.

Verdane Care is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace and welcomes applications from career changers and people returning to work.

**Graz, 22 September 2026**

The new app cuts the median booking time from 94 to 41 seconds and passes the WCAG 2.2 AA audit commissioned from an independent accessibility consultancy.

The company also opened a small engineering hub in Ljubljana, Croatia, to recruit developers who prefer working in the Adriatic time zone. cover_letter_history.content:
Dear Verdane Care hiring team,

I am writing to apply for the Full-Stack Engineer – Patient Experience role. Verdane’s focus on accessible, easy-to-use patient software appeals to me: I first became interested in accessibility when a friend who uses a screen reader showed me how difficult many websites were for her to use.

During my software development internship at Harbourline Media, I built React components and implemented accessibility fixes. I developed a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery, documented it in Storybook and tested it using Jest and React Testing Library.

For my final-year project, Tidewatch, I built a React and TypeScript frontend and a Node.js/Express API that cached data from public weather and tide APIs, with PostgreSQL for user favourites. I tested the app with NVDA and VoiceOver, and it achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. I have also used Next.js in a freelance project for a yoga studio and supported first-year web development students as a teaching assistant.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring this experience to Verdane’s patient-facing products and discuss how I could contribute to the team. Thank you for considering my application.

Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a concise, professional and credible cover letter with a clear progression from accessibility motivation to internship experience and the Tidewatch project. It highlights the strongest supported matches: React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility testing, Jest, React Testing Library, Storybook and Next.js. The letter is appropriately brief for a role where a cover letter is optional. Its main weaknesses are that the opening is somewhat generic and personal, the closing is formulaic, and it does not make the wellness connection explicit even though the candidate built a yoga-studio site. It also does not quantify or emphasize the candidate's First Class final-year result, which could strengthen the application without overstating experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The plain-text structure is ATS-friendly: standard paragraphs, no tables, graphics or unusual formatting, and several relevant keywords appear naturally. React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, Next.js, Storybook, Jest, React Testing Library, NVDA, VoiceOver and Lighthouse are all searchable terms. AI/ATS screening probability is moderate rather than high because the letter does not include terms such as automated testing, unit testing, semantic HTML, responsive design, Git, web security, GDPR or health-data privacy; however, several of these are not supported by the candidate's original information and must not be added. The letter should remain a supplement to the CV rather than attempting to include every job-ad keyword.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns strongly with Verdane Care's accessibility and patient-experience focus. The accessible Tidewatch application, screen-reader testing and Lighthouse score of 100 are particularly relevant to the company's emphasis on accessible, easy-to-use software. The Node.js/Express API and PostgreSQL experience also align with the full-stack scope, while Storybook and Next.js match nice-to-have requirements. The yoga-studio project provides a truthful wellness-sector connection, but the current letter only describes it as a freelance project. The candidate's material does not establish the required 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience: it shows a four-month internship plus freelance, academic and personal project experience. It also does not establish semantic HTML, responsive layouts, end-to-end testing, Git workflows, OWASP/web-security awareness, health-data privacy willingness, German or Croatian, AWS, Docker, or analytics/A-B testing. These are candidate-profile gaps, not defects to solve through wording. Fluent English is demonstrated by the letter itself.
